title: fix(metadata-protocol): ensureOverlayIndex probes before it drops, and reports what it could not enforce (#6418)
body:
Fixes objectstack-ai/objectstack#6418

Ports the probe-first order from the sibling `view-definition-active-index.ts` into `ensureOverlayIndex`, applies it to **both** overlay sections, and replaces the empty `catch` blocks with ADR-0120 D4's disposition. Pure ordering + reporting fix: the key spelling is byte-identical and the dialect fallback stays non-UNIQUE.

## The premise, verified line by line on `origin/main` before implementing

All three claims in the card hold as filed (`protocol.ts` @ `61282f906`):

| claim | verified |
|---|---|
| DROP runs before CREATE | `:2603` `try { await exec("DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_sys_metadata_overlay_active"); } catch { /* best-effort */ }` |
| the degradation regex misses data conflicts | `:2615` `/partial|where clause|syntax/i` — `UNIQUE constraint failed` / `duplicate key value` match none of the three words |
| the catches are empty | `:2619` `// ignore — non-essential optimization`, `:2622` `// "already exists" or anything else: best-effort`, `:2646`, `:2651` |
| the draft section repeats the shape | `:2630`–`:2649`, identical |

One thing the card left implicit that I measured, because it decides how reachable the conflict branch is: `sys-metadata.object.ts` **declares** `idx_sys_metadata_overlay_active` as an *unrestricted, NULL-distinct* `UNIQUE` over `['type','name','organization_id','package_id']`, and `syncDeclaredIndexes` materializes it. The runtime index is therefore a **tightening** in the `COALESCE(package_id, '')` direction — two package-less ACTIVE rows under one `(type, name, organization_id)` are legal for the declared index and rejected by the runtime one. So the conflict path is not only "old databases": it is any database holding that pair, which nothing has ever rejected. That is the same shape #6417 found on `sys_view_definition`, and it is what the new tests seed on real SQLite.

## What changed

**`migrations/partial-index-probe.ts` (new, shared).** The order, stated once: build the tighter index under a throwaway probe name → drop the probe → only now drop the real name and rebuild it. A failure at the probe step has touched nothing, so whatever was protecting the table is still protecting it. It deliberately does **not** report — what is lost when a tightening fails differs per table, and one generic sentence would be true of neither.

`view-definition-active-index.ts` now delegates to it and re-exports `IndexExec` / `classifyIndexFailure` / its status type under their original names, so `index.ts` and its callers see no change. **Its test file is untouched and passes unmodified** — not even the imports needed editing.

**`migrations/overlay-index.ts` (new).** `sys_metadata`'s two indexes, built through that helper, independently — a failure on one no longer decides the other. Each failure is classified and reported at `error`: keep the previous index, name the key that is not enforced and what that costs (`getMetaItem` has no defined answer for which colliding row wins), ship the exact duplicate-listing query, point at `os migrate plan`, never block boot.

**`protocol.ts`.** `ensureOverlayIndex` keeps its driver-resolution walk verbatim and now does nothing else but hand the raw-SQL seam over. Its outer `try/catch` survives for driver *resolution* only; every DDL failure past that point is classified and reported instead of vanishing.

## Two things deliberately NOT changed

- **The key spelling**, byte-identical: `(type, name, organization_id, COALESCE(package_id, ''))`. Pinned as a literal in `pins the key spelling, unchanged by this fix`, so a later "while we are in here" re-keying cannot ride in unnoticed. `sys_metadata`'s bare `organization_id` key part stays the separate, unfiled question the #6666 pricing note names.
- **The dialect fallback stays non-UNIQUE.** One ACTIVE row and one DRAFT row for the same key legitimately coexist here — that coexistence is why `..._overlay_draft` exists at all — so a full UNIQUE would reject legal data. This is the key difference from `sys_view_definition`, and it is now a test (`the dialect fallback is NOT unique, and never drops anything first`) rather than a comment. What *did* change: the fallback is issued with `IF NOT EXISTS` and **no preceding drop**, so it can only ever add an index, never replace a stronger one — and the report says plainly what is and is not enforced.

One correction to the paradigm rather than a copy of it: the shipped duplicate-listing query projects the folded column through its own `COALESCE` (`… AS package_id_key`) instead of bare. A bare projection of a column that appears in `GROUP BY` only inside an expression is rejected by PostgreSQL, and this query has to run on both dialects that can build the index it explains.

## Tests: 30 new cases, real SQLite (`node:sqlite`), and a measured reverse verification

`packages/metadata-protocol`: **700 passed (62 files)**, `driver-sql` 1049 passed, `metadata` 573 passed.

The conflict case is not a mocked throw — it seeds the duplicate pair the declared index admits, runs the migration, and asserts the whole disposition, including that the shipped query really names the offenders on that very database:

```text
✓ a pre-existing duplicate ACTIVE pair blocks the tightening — old index kept, rows named, boot survives
✓ a duplicate DRAFT pair keeps the pre-existing draft index — and the active one still lands
✓ a dialect without partial indexes keeps the original index intact and never downgrades it
✓ MySQL refuses every statement — nothing is touched, and the report says so
✓ the ACTIVE+DRAFT pair stays legal even after BOTH indexes degrade
```

**Reverse verification, direction predicted before running.** Restoring DROP-then-CREATE inside the shared helper: predicted 13 red, all of them old-index-survives pins, **and one predicted GREEN** — the MySQL case, where the mock refuses every statement including the DROP, so the old index survives by accident. That accidental safety is exactly what the card describes ("安全性依赖于一条语法恰好不被接受"), so it must not move in either direction.

Measured: **14 red / 642 green**. The 14th is `a race between the probe and the rebuild is named, not swallowed` — the same probe-order class, which I under-counted rather than mis-predicted. The MySQL case stayed green as predicted. Four of the 14 are `view-definition-active-index.test.ts`'s own pins, re-proved through the shared helper — the extraction did not weaken #6666.

## Verification

- Gates **enumerated one by one from `.github/workflows/lint.yml`**, foreground, under the shared lock: **41 PASS** (`pnpm lint`, `check:slot-lookup`, `check:query-options-erasure`, `check:verify-stand-in`, `check:nul-bytes`, `check:doc-authoring`, `check:docs-audit-scope`, `check:role-word`, `check:quick-reference-counts`, `check:adr-anchors`, `check:org-identifier`, `check:authz-resolver`, `check:service-providers`, `check:route-envelope`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:wildcard-fallthrough`, `check:meta-type-normalized`, `check:init-service-contract`, `check:durability-log-level`, `check:startup-registry-verdict`, `check:objectui-changeset`, `check:release-notes`, `check:release-body`, `check:node-version`, `check:workflow-status-functions`, `check:shard-attestation`, `check:published-files`, `check:engine-double-contract`, `check:kernel-hook-pairs`, `check:resume-authority-declared`, `check:driver-memory-census`, `check:merge-driver`, `check:spec-parsed-alias`, `check:type-check-coverage`, `check:driver-conformance`, `check:stall-guard`, `check:skill-frame-sync`, `check:skill-compatibility`, `check:i18n`, `check:i18n-coverage`, `check:app-nav-i18n`). The three i18n gates first reported `PREREQUISITE NOT MET` and were re-run green after a real build — they measure nothing without one.
- `tsc --noEmit`: **63 errors = exactly the recorded ledger number, zero in any file this PR touches.** `check:type-check-debt` earned its keep here: it caught my unused `dropIndexQuietly` import as a +1 drift, fixed in the second commit.
- Base: cut from `origin/main`, then merged `origin/main` **after PR #6708 landed as `a5d25734c`**, as the dispatch required. The two regions are disjoint in the merged file — #6708's `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` at `:2439`, this PR's `ensureOverlayIndex` at `:2650`.

## Successor pricing for #6602 (`applyRegistryWriteThrough` / `getMetaItems`)

**Easier, marginally — and never harder.** #6602 reads the registry this index guards, and its correctness argument rests on "one ACTIVE row per `(type, name, organization_id, package_id)`". Before this PR that premise could be false *silently* on exactly the deployments #6602 cares about; after it, the premise either holds or the boot said out loud that it does not, with the offending rows named. No shape #6602 touches moves: no key change, no new read path, no change to what a successful boot leaves in the schema. Regions are disjoint (`:2650` here vs `:3284`/`:10514`).

---

**中文摘要**：`ensureOverlayIndex` 原本「先 DROP 后 CREATE」，建失败后无人补回旧索引，两个 catch 全空——在 SQLite/PostgreSQL 上 `sys_metadata` 会静默地一个唯一约束都不剩。本 PR 把 `view-definition-active-index.ts` 的「先探针、后替换」顺序抽成共享 `partial-index-probe.ts`（该模块行为与测试一字未改），active / draft 两段都照此重写，空 catch 换成 ADR-0120 D4 口径：保留旧索引、点名未生效的键、附上列出冲突行的查询、指向 `os migrate plan`、绝不阻断启动。⛔ 未改键的拼写；降级目标仍是非唯一复合索引（active 与 draft 合法共存，全量 UNIQUE 会误伤），但改为 `IF NOT EXISTS` 且不先删，只能新增、不可能替换掉更强的索引。反向验证先定方向后跑：预判 13 红 + MySQL 那条「偶然安全」保持绿，实测 14 红（第 14 条同属 probe-order 类，我漏计），绿的那条如预判。
